A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BinaryDM despite the changed title and substantial method revision. All 30 pages of v2 and 18 pages of v4, including figures, equations, tables, appendices and v2's checklist, were readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-generation experiments, component ablations and efficiency measurements in Tables 1–18, with additional generated samples and feature analyses.

after.justification: v4 reports original experiments for the revised BinaryDM, including generation benchmarks, efficiency measurements and transition-specific ablations in Tables 1–10.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces persistent Learnable Multi-basis Binarization with Evolvable-Basis Binarization: a new regularization loss suppresses the second basis during training, and that basis is subsequently removed for single-basis inference. This changes the objective, training stages and deployed weights, rather than merely renaming LMB. LRM remains, while v2's separate progressive warm-up disappears from the described procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate unconditional generation on CIFAR-10, LSUN-Bedrooms, LSUN-Churches and FFHQ, and conditional generation on ImageNet, at the same resolutions. FFHQ and additional ImageNet sampler results already appear in v2's appendix; their inclusion in v4's main tables does not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: LSQ comparisons disappear from FFHQ and all three ImageNet sampler comparisons: compare v2 Tables 3, 7 and 8 with v4 Tables 2 and 3. This substantially narrows comparator coverage. Q-DM and TDQ already appeared in v2 Table 10; v4 retains their 1-bit comparisons but drops their 2-bit comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 changes the input/output layers from full precision to 8-bit, while BinaryDM evaluations switch from nominal 1.1-bit to 1-bit weights. Table 4 changes from separate component ablations to cumulative additions, and new experiments vary regularization strength and transition timing. The basic metrics, evaluation sample counts, batch sizes and approximately 200K training budget remain.

E4.justification: v4 adds weight-evolution trajectories and regularization-strength/transition-timing studies, and revises component and placement ablations. The LRM dimensionality sweep is retained, moving from v2 Table 13 to v4 Table 10. Earlier analyses of additional bases, progressive warm-up, LRM at other precisions, mixed-precision controls, QALoRA and training duration are removed.

E5.justification: v2's checklist item 7 states that random seeds were fixed for all experiments; v4 omits this disclosure. Neither specifies repeated-run counts or defined confidence-interval/significance-testing procedures. The reporting change does not establish a change in actual randomization or run counts.

E6.justification: Benchmark results are extensively replaced. For example, BinaryDM's CIFAR-10 FID changes from 25.83 at W1.1A4 to 87.77 at W1A4, and LSUN-Bedrooms FID changes from 7.11 to 7.74; these involve changed methods and precision settings, not same-setting regressions. The Bedrooms baseline FID changes from 39.69 to 10.87, and the retained LSQ W2A8 entry changes from 6.08 to 6.48. Ablation results are also added, replaced and removed.

T1.justification: v4 formally defines the new scaling-factor regularizer in Equation 9 and incorporates it into the total objective in Equation 15. The diffusion equations, PCA formulation and existing binarizer gradient derivations are retained. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion redefine the principal contribution from persistent multi-basis weights plus progressive warm-up to an evolution process producing single-basis weights. Headline claims change from W1.1A4 with 9.3-fold operation and 24.8-fold storage savings to W1A4 with 15.2-fold and 29.2-fold savings. LRM and the first-binarization-method claim remain.

C2.justification: v4 explains extra bases as temporary initialization aids and selective placement as reducing transition instability; v2 emphasized persistent representation capacity and storage tradeoffs. v4 removes the activation-quantization limitation, the qualification that LRM is less effective than MSE at 4-bit, and the discussion distinguishing BinaryDM's full-model, original-data training from EfficientDM's LoRA and data-free setup.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 changes the reported GPU from A800 80GB to A100 40GB and revises the CPU specification. New ablation tables disclose regularization coefficients and transition iterations, while the old warm-up implementation details disappear. v2's promise of supplementary code is also absent in v4; the PDFs do not establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: v4 adds high-order residual quantization, BiLLM and DB-LLM references to distinguish EBB's temporary bases from approaches retaining extra bases at inference. GPTQ, TFMQ-DM and TDQ references are also added. The broader diffusion/quantization review and first-binarization positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v4 retitles the paper and substantially rewrites the contribution narrative and Section 3.2 around EBB, removing the separate training-strategy subsection. FFHQ and additional sampler discussions move into the main results, the experimental appendix is reorganized and condensed, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: The overview is redrawn for EBB, the weight histogram becomes a multi-stage display, and the earlier tradeoff, detail-crop and warm-up figures disappear. Appendix benchmark tables are merged into main Tables 2–3, ablation displays are restructured, and sample grids are replaced with compact multi-bit panels. Figure placement and the document template also change substantially.

improvement.justification: EBB addresses v2's persistent extra-basis inference cost, supported by new transition ablations. However, v4 removes substantial LSQ comparisons and important qualifications about EfficientDM. Its retained FFHQ superiority claim now contradicts Table 2: W1A8 BinaryDM has sFID 10.74 versus W8A8 Q-Diffusion's 10.01, whereas v2 Table 7 supported that comparison with 8.14. The methodological gains coexist with reduced comparative evidence and weaker claim accuracy, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
